claims.text: FeNiCrMn HEA has been produced and optimized primarily for corrosion resistance.
The FeNiCrMn HEA contains limited Co.
The FeNiCrMn HEA likely exhibits microstructural heterogeneities because of its multi-element composition.
Localized nanoindentation can measure hardness and elastic modulus across different regions of FeNiCrMn HEA.
The relevant local microstructural heterogeneities may include grain boundaries, phase distributions, and precipitates.
Such local microstructural variations arise from the alloy's multi-principal-element composition.
Compositional complexity and associated lattice distortions in HEAs produce spatial heterogeneity.
Spatial heterogeneities alter local bonding environments.
Changes in dislocation mobility and local bonding cause microscale variations in hardness and elastic modulus.
Nanoindentation of FeNiCrMn will reveal significant local variations in hardness and elastic modulus.
The local hardness and elastic-modulus variations will correlate with microstructural heterogeneities.
Localized sites will exhibit significantly higher or lower hardness and elastic modulus than the sample-wide average.
Bulk mechanical tests such as tensile tests report averaged properties and do not resolve contributions from localized microstructural heterogeneities.
Surface quality and preparation-induced artifacts may affect the measured local variation.
Heterogeneities smaller than the nanoindenter's spatial resolution may not be detected.

contradictions.description: The nominal FeNiCrMn system and the stated motivation imply a Co-free alloy, whereas the material description says it has 'limited Co content,' implying possible Co presence.
